ShortDescription.Value: Ski resorts: lifts that fit your terrain, runs on natural or machine-made snow, lodges, ski school and patrol, a resort planner, resort economics, and merging your own buildings.

Publish.LongDescription:
[Trailer](https://youtu.be/NJvzaxwGfa4) | [Features](https://youtu.be/mkysRTD0zmQ)
**Build a ski resort in Cities: Skylines II.**
Draw lifts up your mountain and runs down it. Natural or machine-made snow opens the runs. Guests ski (counted, not shown, yet), buy tickets and lessons, and the resort draws tourists to your city. No mods required, but Anarchy and Move It are highly recommended, along with Write Everywhere.
## Highlights - **Four lifts, one tool.** Fixed-grip triple chairlift, detachable quad chairlift, gondola and aerial tram. The tool plans numbered towers over your terrain, and you can move them. Chairs and cabins ride the rope. - **Runs on real snow.** Groomed or natural, with floodlights. Snow guns build a 2 m base that keeps a run open through a thaw. Each run is rated from its hardest pitch, in North American or European grading. It opens at 3 ft (91 cm) of snow on 60 % of the run. - **Night on the mountain.** Floodlights come on at dusk, like the street lights. Groomers work the cat tracks from dusk to dawn. - **Resort Planner.** Outline a mountainside and get a plan of linked runs, cat tracks and lifts. - **Seasons.** Snow melts in spring, runs close, and chairlifts and gondolas stop. Lodges and the school close off-season. The aerial tram keeps running for summer sightseeing. Northern and Southern Hemisphere maps both work. - **Lodges, Ski School, Ski Patrol and a Ski Bus Depot.** Five lodges, a school, two patrol buildings, and a coach stop in town for a hill too far away. - **Merge your own buildings.** A landmark, signature or recreation building near the runs can join the resort as a lodge. - **One hub.** Attraction, runs, lifts, guests, finances and history, with every problem and its cause. - **A resort economy.** Tickets, season passes, lessons and lodge spend against running costs. Set the ticket and season pass prices with sliders in the hub. To raise ticket tolerance, build better lodges. The resort tourism bonus raises the whole city's attractiveness, as an airport does.
## Requirements Cities: Skylines II 1.6 (tested on 1.6.4f1). No DLC or other mod required.
## Getting started Open the Ski Resort hub (button at the top left). Its Start card lists the four steps to a first resort.
## Good to know - Skiers are counted, not visually simulated. Chairs and cabins move but carry no riders. (Post Park Adventures, I will try my best to at least get Cims on the chairlifts) - Lifts are built on the game's power-line network, so the game shows some power-line details for them, such as a Transformer section in station panels. Like a real lift, each base station needs low-voltage power. The game refuses a high-voltage line at a lift. - The Mountain Hut, Chalet and Summit lodges, both patrol buildings, the Ski School and the fixed-grip and tram top stations keep the slope they stand on. Build them into the hillside with the terrain tools or Move It. - Bulldozing a Welcome Sign deletes every run linked to it and refunds no run fee. A warning comes first. - Two lifts of the same type cannot cross. A cat track cannot pass under a lift that is already built, so build cat tracks first. - Before uninstalling, use "Delete all ski resort content" in the mod's Options, then save the city. - Resorts cost money all year and earn in winter. Welcome to ski resort economics!
## Guides and details - [Docs site](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort): guides, every number, settings and troubleshooting. - Start with the [Resort Quickstart](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort/quickstart/) and the [Lifts guide](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort/guides/lifts/). - Bug reports: the [Paradox forum thread](https://forum.paradoxplaza.com/forum/threads/modular-ski-resort.1949673/) or the [Discord thread](https://discord.com/channels/263634513861541888/1570379334672326736). Paste the text from the Copy diagnostics button in the mod's Options. - [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/theotherwildcathighboy/ModularSkiResort)
## Credits - Modular Golf Course Pack by joergeske: the modular recreation idea this mod grew from. - Meapy's Tourism Overhaul: studied for how tourism and attractions work. Not required. Works alongside this mod. - Logo and in-game icon by [Lexa](https://lexakeenen.com/). - All assets (chairs, lodges, patrol huts) are based on [real places](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort/credits/#asset-inspirations). - Built with Claude (Anthropic) for decompilation, prefab work and asset generation. Direction and many, many hours of testing by the author. - [Full credits and licenses](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort/credits/).
Publish.ChangeLog:
**What you may notice on load:** - Some runs may change difficulty band, mostly from black to blue, under the new rating rule (Runs, below). - The season pass is now set as a price. Your Options value carries over as that price. Above 4 day tickets' worth, fewer households buy a pass.
**Saves:** - Lifts, runs, cat tracks and resort buildings built from now on remember the version that built them, so a later update can bring older ones up to date. - A city saved with 1.0.2 still loads in 1.0.1, but that version forgets which version built what.
**Sync resort:** - When an update changes how resort objects should look, the hub's Attraction view shows "Sync resort" with the objects of that ski area that are out of date. The first one: Patrol Huts placed before 1.0.1 get their firewood pile. - Each object can be skipped or kept as it is. Sync is free and has no undo.
**Prices:** - Sliders in the Finances view for the lift ticket price and the season pass price. - The ticket price shows one demand word, from unaffected to very low. Its tooltip says how many fewer guests come. - Season pass price: 20 to 2,000, default 400. Up to 4 day tickets' worth, every household that wants a pass buys one. Above that, fewer do. - Ticket tolerance reads the same everywhere: 40, 60 with a Chalet Lodge, 80 with a Swanky Summit or Grand Lodge. - Tooltips name the lever: "To raise ticket tolerance, build better lodges."
**Hub:** - Sliders for snow gun and light spacing on runs, and for tree density. - History: a "This season so far" block with totals, the best month, the average ticket and the income and cost mix, against last season. - Snow report on the Welcome Sign card and in the status tooltip: summit and base, snow depth, temperature, new snow and season snowfall. - "Closed for the summer" in the off-season, instead of "Too warm for snow". - Lodges and the ski school closed for the off-season are no longer a problem. The school row says "Closed: off-season". - "Ski-day cars not arriving" names the main cause: no route, stuck on the way, never left home, or out of time. - The merge card shows only with the hub open. Tiers the city cannot pay for are blocked. - The build strip keeps its size: a tab click never closes it, the chevron does. - One height for all text buttons. The Resort Planner's features are check boxes. - The Start card says a lift needs low-voltage power. - The full problem list moves the view down instead of covering it. - "Welcome Sign stopped" without an empty colon, "1 acre" in the singular, and merged buildings under readable names.
**Tourism:** - Resort tourism bonus: ski areas raise the whole city's attractiveness, as an airport does. Up to 10 % by default (Options, 0 to 20 %, 0 turns it off). It brings tourists to the city, not skiers to the runs. - New Attraction view rows: tourists in the city, guests at resort hotels (merged buildings), and the tourist spending the ski area draws. - "City tourist income" is now "Tourist spending" and shows under Tourism Overhaul too. It is spending at city businesses, so it stays out of the resort's net.
**Runs:** - Blue runs are easier to get. A short steep pitch keeps a run black only when its own steep stretch is 40 m or longer. A narrow steep spot, such as a cat track bank, no longer forces black. - While you draw, the rating reads "(so far)" until the outline is closed. - Black and double black shading is easier to see in evening light. - A run that costs more than the city has shows the game's no-money icon. - Run labels change color when you switch the run grading. - Runs that cannot be rated are pale orange, apart from the orange ski route.
**Snow:** - Snow guns build a 2 m base, then stop, and start again below 1.95 m. Runs stay open longer through a thaw. - Made snow melts at the game's own rate, on runs and cat tracks alike. A run and a cat track over the same height open together, at any game speed. - Some narrow runs that never opened on made snow now do. - A cat track pays snowmaking for the part of it the guns work on. - After a load the snow guns continue as they were: no plume flash, no missed bill.
**Groomers and lights:** - Groomers work from dusk to dawn. They arrive one after another, nearest first, and leave at dawn. - A groomer leaves a cat track below 80 % snow cover and returns at 87.5 %, so it no longer drives on grass. - On short cat tracks, groomers rest at each end. - Run floodlights, snow gun beacons and groomer lamps turn on at dusk, like street lights, instead of at 18:00.
**Lift tool:** - Lifts can cross at 15°, down from 20°. - Right click a tower to remove it. Right click elsewhere or Esc still steps back. - A line the city cannot pay for says so.
**Buildings:** - Placing a lodge, the ski school or a patrol building no longer opens the Happiness view. - A merged building's goods trade no longer makes the ski area's efficiency jump off-season. - The Ski Bus roof carries one roundel that reads right from every side. - Menu and Find It icons show the building alone, like vanilla.
**Options:** - The ski area radius is measured from the Welcome Sign in a straight line, not along roads.
